title: Generalized building B(Σ) = G ×^K A
body_html:
Generalized building $\BSigma = G \times^K A$

Let $K$ be a $K$-cosheaf on $A$ (see [[node:building.K_cosheaf]]).

Definition. The generalized building attached to $K$ is $$\BSigma \;:=\; G \times^K A.$$

Concretely, $\BSigma = (G \times A) / \sim$ with $$(g, x) \sim (h, y) \iff \exists\, n \in N \text{ such that } n \cdot x = y \text{ and } g^{-1} h n \in K_x.$$

This is an instance of [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_GxP_X]] with $G' \rightsquigarrow N$, $X' \rightsquigarrow A$, and $P \rightsquigarrow K$. By CW structure and QFD property on G ×^P X', $\BSigma$ inherits a unique regular CW complex structure for which the $G$-action is cellular, and $A$ is a quasi-fundamental domain.

Extension to the full Bruhat–Tits building

By [[node:equivariant_sheaves.induction_universal_property|induction by stages]], the cosheaf $K$ extends to a cosheaf (still denoted $K$) on $\mathcal{B}(G')$ via $K_{g x} := g K_x g^{-1}$ for $g \in G'$, $x \in A$, and $$\BSigma \;=\; G \times^K \mathcal{B}(G').$$

Comparison with $\mathcal{B}(G')$

When $K_x = G'_x$, the lower bound of the $K$-condition is tight, and $\BSigma = G \times^{G'_\bullet} A \;=\; \mathcal{B}(G')$. In general $\BSigma$ is a refinement of $\mathcal{B}(G')$ "puffed up" by larger compact opens. The chain complex Chain complex C_•(Φ, V) of φ-isotypic chains is built from $\BSigma$, not from $\mathcal{B}(G')$.
